headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty ended mixed as investors weighed a Fed rate hike against NSE IPO buzz.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: The Federal Reserve's interest rate hike influenced investor sentiment and market volatility.
Anticipation and news regarding the potential NSE IPO provided a mixed trigger for the indices.
Geopolitical concerns regarding US sanctions on Russia led to a cautious trading environment.
Mixed global cues and profit booking in specific sectors resulted in a non-directional market close.
whatHappening: Over 150 stocks including IRCTC and BEML have record dates for dividends and splits this week.
Ten midcap stocks have reported their highest quarterly profits in the last ten quarters.
Market participants are tracking GIFT Nifty and Asian markets for opening cues on Monday.
Focus for the upcoming week remains on crude oil prices and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) activity.

summary: The Indian markets concluded the last trading session on September 17 with a mixed performance as investors balanced a Fed rate hike against NSE IPO buzz. While the market remains closed for the weekend, attention is shifting to over 150 stocks facing corporate actions like dividends and splits. Traders are now looking toward Monday's opening, guided by GIFT Nifty signals and geopolitical developments involving US-Russia sanctions.
